assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only classroom-of-the-elite:horikita-suzune@original-light-novels-through-year-2#cote-y2-03-horikita-leadership-self-authorship-and-class-formation, the canonical Year-2 specialist synthesis COTE_Y2_03_HORIKITA_LEADERSHIP_SELF_AUTHORSHIP_AND_CLASS_FORMATION.md at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese original light novels: frozen Year 1 (summarized through the Year-1 specialist's claim transitions), Y2V01-Y2V12.5 volume by volume, Volume 0 at its retrospective position and the Year 2 Official Guidebook Second List. Year 3 narrative evidence is excluded by the monograph and was not used. The companion ledgers it routes to (character, voice, relationship, ethics, ordinary-life and the behavioral reconstruction protocol) are not curated on this subject and were not used. The monograph's own readiness and confidence statements are inputs, not conclusions. The evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Year-1 states only as the baseline the monograph summarizes (static-merit early self through the Y1V11.5 identity break); Year-2 states located per volume: V01 reciprocal first-year design, V02 presidency goal and the first Koenji bargain, V03-V04 island exam, V04.5, V05 Kushida preservation and Airi's expulsion, V06 Kushida compact, Haruka confrontation and Ryuen alliance, V07-V08, Volume 0 (retrospective, no new Horikita state), V09 presidency and the Kiryuin/Kiriyama settlement, V09.5, V10 Ike correction and Ibuki friction, V11, V12 0-10 defeat, V12.5 provisional Class A and Ayanokoji's unannounced departure, and Second List. Key scenes carry spine/paragraph or evidence-cluster locators; others are volume-level. V05 and V06 are separate capability states: pre-V06 states lack the self-authored Kushida compact.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: A governing account ('constitutional developmental pluralism', sections 1 and 19) with three separated independence predicates (judgment established, political authorship established, system reproduction open) and an explicit decision family (section 33.2: governing obligation, role versus preference, specialist input, reasons, choice, visible responsibility, revision). The account says what changes her response: jurisdiction and scope (Koenji, Kiryuin/Kiriyama), explicit obligation, domain expertise (Ike, Hirata, Kei), relationship-specific cost (Ibuki, Kushida), information she lacks (Ayanokoji's timetable) and chronology. It predicts her mistakes as well as her prudence: developmental optimism that makes nonconsenting third parties pay (V05 Airi), the reckless promise to Haruka, the plan Ike corrects and the genuine V12 defeat. It stops at named forks (section 33.6).

Year 2 is traced volume by volume with located state changes: imposed Kushida preservation (V05) versus self-authored compact (V06, spine14 para0470-0525), office acquired (V09), defeat without collapse (V12, spine17 para0473-0542), assumed shared future versus unannounced separation (V12.5, spine21 para0083-0105). A Year-1 to Year-2 claim-transition ledger (sections 2 and 36) states which earlier claims are preserved, strengthened, revised or rejected. Volume 0 is held as retrospective recontextualization, not a Horikita state. Limit: Year-1 states are summarized as a baseline only, not located per volume on this evidence.

Section 32 describes a stable written register (complete sentences, the feminine endings ～わ, ～よ and ～かしら, judgment-oriented diction, explicit distinctions, limited cushioning), the speech acts Year 2 adds (asking for judgment, owning a decision, admitting a narrow error, acknowledging uncertainty, practical care), relationship-specific variance (no counterfeit warmth with Kushida, lower ceremony only with Ibuki, precise care with Ayanokoji) and explicit simulation prohibitions. Very few of her own lines are quoted; the voice ledger it cites is not curated here. The register is constrained by description rather than attested lines.

Low-stakes surfaces appear only around relationships: school-trip rivalry and play with Ibuki (V08), ordinary teasing and the V10 low-stakes exchange with Ayanokoji (spine14 para0390-0412), practical concern in her care for him, and the V12.5 unclassified bodily response (spine19 para0131-0175). The monograph routes ordinary life to an uncurated ledger. Daily routine, hobbies, study habits and solitary life are not described.

Section 33.4 gives per-relationship support and prohibitions, grounded in located sections: Ayanokoji (judgment reciprocity, recognition desire, care, timetable asymmetry; no obedience or romance closure), Kushida (hostile cooperation for reasons she can own; no gratitude demand or warm reconciliation), Ibuki (adversarial friendship, lower ceremony, moral friction without immunity), Sudo (peer-like respect after rejection), Koenji (bounded bargain, no title to his full capacity), plus Ryuen (witnessed, scoped alliance without trust), Haruka (standing dissent), Ike (correction from below), Hirata and Kei (complementary authority) and Nanase (refused coup). It explains what each relation changes. Transfer to an unsampled classmate is not established.

Located interior states are few and late: regarding Ayanokoji as indispensable (V11 spine20 para0060), admitting she wanted his praise (V12), loneliness at his unannounced exit (V12.5 spine21 para0097-0105) and an unclassified heart-rate response (V12.5 spine19). Most of the account infers motive from decisions; the monograph itself keeps the category of her attachment open and warns against backdating recognition desire.

Political and interpersonal conflict is the best-located domain: defining conditions rather than accepting a vague covenant (Koenji, V02), refusing Sudo's proposal to break that contract and rebargaining instead (V05), sustaining disagreement with Ayanokoji under catastrophic stakes (V05), owning the judgment while narrowing the apology to Haruka (V06), converting rivalry into a written, teacher-observed alliance (Ryuen, V06), binding a predecessor without invented punishment (V09), asking for trust while admitting uncertainty (V10). The model says which response follows from scope, obligation and standing. Physical confrontation is mentioned only in the Ibuki relationship and is not modeled.

Section 30 gives a deliberation structure (who is treated as disposable, who bears the cost of preservation, who authors the preserved person's future), a narrowed principle (anti-disposability is epistemic caution before irreversible removal, not a never-expel rule), a jurisdiction question ('what am I entitled to decide for this person?') and a dirty-hands rule (later success does not cleanse V05). It separates independent, legitimate and just choice (section 0.4) and predicts the characteristic ethical failure. Section 33.5 says the structure is supported where the final branch may stay open, as in a friend-versus-class conflict.

Only the observation that she can enter a petty, bodily, competitive or playful register with Ibuki and exchange low-stakes teasing with Ayanokoji. Humor is otherwise unanalyzed. Bounded canon questions only.

One canonical Horikita-centered specialist covering the whole Year-2 boundary with routes to immutable volume readings. Year 1 enters only as summarized claim transitions, several sections are volume-level without paragraph locators, and the companion character, voice, relationship, ethics and ordinary-life ledgers and the behavioral reconstruction protocol that the monograph names as authoritative companions are not curated on this subject. The evaluator inspected no primary source.

Affirmative limits are explicit: the mandatory abstention zones (section 33.6), the open handoff states (Y1H-012, Y1H-014 and Y1H-015 partial; Y1H-016 still open, section 38), simulation prohibitions for voice (section 32.6), relationship prohibitions (section 33.4) and ten rejected or downgraded reductions (section 34), including the puppet reading, Class A as proof of independence and 'becoming nicer'.

States are bound to named volumes, Volume 0 is placed retrospectively without creating a Horikita belief, Second List is treated as a boundary audit rather than future certification, and Year 3 is excluded. Load-bearing scenes carry spine/paragraph or evidence-cluster locators (for example Y2V10-E060 to E063, Y2V12-E086 to E105, Y2SL-E013 to E028); other sections are volume-level only.

conditions: Illustrative Japanese or translated lines only, never presented as quotation.
Register follows section 32: complete sentences, controlled ～わ, ～よ and ～かしら endings, judgment-oriented diction and limited cushioning, with the Year-2 speech acts used only at Year-2 states.
The interlocutor is a sampled relation and the relation-specific register applies: no counterfeit warmth with Kushida, lowered ceremony only with Ibuki, precise practical care with Ayanokoji.
Not permanently cold, slang-heavy, a generic tsundere or pleading for Ayanokoji's approval.
scenario_readiness.note: The section 32 register description and its prohibitions constrain illustrative Japanese output for sampled relationships; few attested lines are quoted, so output is illustrative, never quotation.

conditions: Chronology is one named Year-2 state, defaulting to the Second List boundary; V05 states lack the V06 compact and the V09 office, and pre-V12.5 states assume Ayanokoji remains.

The interlocutor is a sampled relation (Ayanokoji, Kushida, Ibuki, Sudo, Koenji, Ryuen, Haruka, Ike, Hirata, Kei). Transfer to an unsampled classmate is a separate, lower-confidence condition using the decision family without invented history.
The situation is a leadership, bargaining, jurisdiction, correction or responsibility problem inside the school system.

Her response to a genuine Ayanokoji failure, Ibuki versus a severe class duty, Koenji contribution beyond a bargain, post-transfer class performance and the category of her attachment to Ayanokoji are output as open forks.
She does not know Ayanokoji's departure timetable or the Volume 0 genealogy before the source gives them to her.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named Year-2 state from Y2V01 to Second List, defaulting to Second List; Year-1 states only at the summarized baseline level; no Year-3 events.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Located classmates and rivals in their recorded relation: Ayanokoji as collaborator and valued judge, Kushida as hostile self-interested cooperator, Ibuki as adversarial friend, Sudo as developed peer, Koenji as bounded counterparty, Ryuen as scoped ally without trust; an unsampled classmate only at lower confidence.
setting_constraints: Advanced Nurturing High School: class, special examinations and student council
No adult, occupational or post-graduation setting
No romance resolution with Ayanokoji or anyone else
Named abstention zones end in an open fork

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded counterfactuals in school leadership, bargaining and sampled relationships at a named Year-2 state are supported; the named forks end in abstention.

Low-stakes behavior is located only as relational friction with Ibuki and Ayanokoji; daily routine and ordinary social life are not described in this evidence. This bounds the evidence set, not Horikita's ordinary life.

conditions: Questions of expulsion, preservation, distributive cost, consent, jurisdiction, promise scope and responsibility inside the school system, using section 30.
Output represents role obligation, relationship cost, alternatives and public responsibility; where section 33.5 leaves the branch open, the final choice is an open fork.
The V05 state may reproduce the cost-externalizing error; V06 and later states apply the self-authorship correction.
scenario_readiness.note: The deliberation structure is explicit and predicts both care and characteristic failure; branch outcomes in untested severe conflicts stay open.
The evidence affirmatively keeps her attachment to Ayanokoji unclassified (romantic, familial, rivalrous or other) and records only that she rejected Sudo. Romantic behavior would be invention.

conditions: School-institutional roles only: class leader and student-council president, using the V02 bargain, V06 alliance, V09 settlement and V10 correction precedents.
Office is exercised through scope, constituency, entitlement and non-retaliation, not predecessor imitation.
Institutional stresses not present in Year 2 are open; no adult work context is modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Class leadership and student-council office are the monograph's center; institutional stresses absent from Year 2 remain open.

known_limits.statement: How Horikita responds to a genuine Ayanokoji failure, defeat or loss of control is an explicit abstention zone; no Year-2 event tests it.
Post-transfer class performance without Ayanokoji's hidden security is prospective at Second List; Class A is achievement, not certification.
Friendship with Ibuki changes the cost of a decision without establishing whether it overrides a severe class duty in an untested case.
Her desire for Ayanokoji's recognition and the V12.5 bodily response are not classified as romantic or any other stable category.
Whether Koenji accepts a new high-cost contribution without an explicit bargain is open; the evidence supports bargaining, not command.
Resilience of her presidency under institutional stresses absent from Year 2 is open (Y1H-015 partial).
At every Year-2 state she does not know when Ayanokoji will leave, and Volume 0's genealogy is reader knowledge, not hers.
Year-1 states are available only as the summarized baseline and claim transitions in this evidence, not volume-located behavior.
The character, voice, relationship, ethics and ordinary-life ledgers and the behavioral reconstruction protocol the monograph names as companions are not curated on this subject.
Daily routine, hobbies, study habits, humor and solitary life are not described.
Very few of her own lines are quoted; voice rests on register description.
